[[VIDEOID:24f288830a6159a895146c8f7ec02c10]] I was pretty excited to pick up one of these Opal dispensers. Here are my findings.

Personally I looked past the 1.8lb ice capacity because it could theroeticly regenerate completely a little over an hour. If you are purchasing for it’s “claimed 38lbs of ice per day" or 1.58lbs per hour, it has never gotten close. That rating 38lbs is in a perfect lab environment. With the unit sitting in the same place as my old Opal 1.0 it makes the same amount of ice. If you ever host people often at your home, this unit will not keep up or have the initial ice capacity. The unit tells me that I need to "descale" about every 3 days. Despite always running distilled water and using the Opal descale kit.

The ice storage container is not very well insulated. The ice melts extremely quickly. The ice also gets stuck on the chute/ramp that dumps it into the ice storage, resulting in false "ice bin full." Then when you want to get some ice, you find that all ice melted and it did not make more.

The dispenser aspect has a mind of its own. The manual states that it will continue to dispense "a few moments after", (about 5 seconds )okay that's fine. I have found it will be several minutes later, it starts to phantom dispense and dump ice all over the counter.

It does though make great nugget ice when it works 75% of the time and that is worth at least 3 stars.

In the end either wait for the next Opal dispenser or just get an Opal 2.0.

It's working and I saved a ton over getting another washer. I also like the tiny hose that is used to empty the pump housing before removing the threaded cap for cleaning. No more water on the floor every time I check the pump for lint and debris. I have another similar machine and am going to buy another one of these pumps to have on hand as a spare.

The pump went out on my second washer and I bought another one of these pumps. The original pump on the second machine was black plastic. The installation went much smoother this time even though there was the same issue with the discharge hose being a very tight fit. By applying a water soluble lubricant to the pump outlet and the o-ring on the hose plus using a bit of force, the connection was made.

Looking back, I should have changed the o-ring on the hose of the first machine to one with a slightly thinner rubber part. Possibly an R-15 o-ring and some better lubricant.

This knob does NOT replace the timer knob - the timer knob is the one that let's you select different wash cycles (such as Cottons or Delicates), and within those cycles, heavy or light cycles. Although the part numbers for timer knobs vary across GE models, the item listed here will NOT function as a timer knob on ANY GE model. It has no teeth to interface with the timer dial.

This knob IS a GE part, however. But this part has a small black line on one end - an indicator line - that is not shown in the photo. What this knob replaces are the other knobs on your GE washer, often to the left of the timer knob. These let you do things like choose between a second rinse cycle and just one, or set the load size at small or large. They usually have a small black indicator line at the end.

I ordered this part based on the image displayed, and the item title Washing machine timer knob. I got a genuine GE part, with a part number matching the one displayed here WH01X10061. This would be fine, but what I needed to replace was the timer knob.

The second time through, I used a GE appliance parts site. This directed me to part number WH01X10310. When it came, it was indeed a timer knob, complete with the clip to install. Now my washer is fixed. Since the price of the part listed here was mostly a shipping charge that is non-refundable, and since they did send me the correct part number, I cannot return it. So I guess I have a spare if one of the selector knobs ever breaks. They rarely do, because they don't have teeth to wear down like timer knobs do.

I ordered this to replace the drain pump on my LG WM2016CW washer. Installation took about 1/2 hour, but I decided to clean out the drain hoses while I was at it. It's not the same as the OEM pump I removed (at least not on mine) but it fit perfectly. It does seem slightly louder during operation, although that could just be me paying attention to the new pump.
Here are some installation tips...
1. Follow the suggestion on other reviews and remove the pump from the bottom of the washer. Just tip the washer back against the wall, make sure it's secure and won't tip forward, and slide underneath the front to work on it.
2. The small cover for the drain and filter screen at the lower left front corner of the washer needs to be removed first. There's one screw holding the cover, and two screws behind that attaching the pump.
3. When you remove the pump, note the orientation of the pump to the housing. The housing has multiple screw holes available that allows the pump to be positioned at different angles. Use the existing screw holes for the replacement pump. It's easy to see which holes in the housing had the three screws in them.
4. While you're down there, I'd recommend taking off the black drain hose from the base of the tub and cleaning it out. This also gives you access to the tank level pressure switch tube. Mine had some crud built up in them.

I've been using the original design Nespresso machines for about 3 years. I like them so much I have two Pixie systems located at different houses. The pods are not cheap. This accessory seemed interesting and would allow me to try various types of expresso coffee at a much lower cost than the Nespresso pods. So, I ordered it.

The kit came in a simple cardboard box. Inside there were two stainless steel capsules, a small brush, 2 extra rubber O-rings and a finger Mit to cover for your thumb and index finger.

I'm not going to go into a description of the components, those are visible on the webpage. I'll just talk about my experience.

For the trial, I purchased a bag of pre-ground Starbucks Expresso coffee which showed an expresso machine on the front of the package. There are many types of expressos sold at the supermarket, but you cannot view the grind before you buy. I knew this could be a problem as the grind for expresso has to be very fine in order to extract the most flavor.

I started by putting the Starbuck's coffee into the capsule. You need to leave enough clear space at the top of the capsule for the cap with its extended screen section to fit down against the coffee. It would have been nice if the company had put a reference ring around the capsule to tell you how far this cap extends. As it is you have to overfill the capsule and tamp it down to the right level - sometimes taking some coffee away, sometimes adding some.

For the first test, I overfilled the capsule a little and gently tamped it down to the right height using the metal measuring cup - I think they used to supply a small tamper. I turned the machine on, and it ran easily but with very little crema and a light color. A failure.

I ran this test 3 more times, each time increasing the pressure I used for tamping down the coffee. By the last test I was tamping as hard as I could with the cup, I had some crema and much darker coffee. It tasted fairly strong, so I made my standard Latte. 2 Expresso shots and about 7 ounces of frothed milk. This was weak and unsatisfying. So, I think the coffee particle size was too large.

So, I borrowed a simple whirling coffee grinder which featured a spinning blade. When grinding coffee with this type of machine, you vary the particle size by varying the time you let the machine run - a longer run time makes finer particles. I also opened a real capsule of Nespresso to examine the particle size they used. I tried to make my particles that size by eye.

I did get the capsule to work by experimenting with grind size. But, over that time, the machine shut off mid pump a number of times because it couldn't pass the water through the capsule - possibly damaging to the machine. And even now when I have a mix that works, it takes time to prepare 2 capsules and, I have to clean up the mess. Also, this coffee doesn't taste as good as Nespresso. So, I may have to buy another one-pound bag of some other brand to try.

To streamline the process an adjustable coffee grinder would probably work for particle size. And I'd have to work on my tamping to get the right compaction in the capsule.

This experiment turned out a lot different than I thought. Switching back and forth between coffee types is more complicated and expensive when you have to buy a pound of each coffee. And for me, that's the beauty of Nespresso - changing coffee flavors is as quick as just loading another pre-measured, pre-tested capsule into the machine - it works every time. This product is well made, and I think it is capable of good results, but it is not what I expected.

Instead of repairing the old GE dishwasher again, it seemed like a good idea to buy a new Maytag and enjoy the reliability for which the brand was famous. Wrong! It was a fairly good dishwasher, in spite of its minor flaws, from July 2019 when purchased and installed until July 2021 when it suddenly stopped pumping water to the arms. After consulting Maytag's website, I booked an appointment with the factory authorized repair service. The repair technician determined that the motor and control board must be replaced. The warranty apparently covers the motor, although the service consultation is the owner's responsibility since the unit is over 1 year old. The warranty saved me approx. $100 of the total cost of repair. I paid $447.23 in advance for the repair, and the repair service ordered parts. Shortly thereafter, I received notice that the control panel was on backorder, then two weeks later another message that the part is indefinitely unavailable. Now I am out the cost of a new Maytag dishwasher, the cost of the repair which has not been performed, which is about $100 less than the original purchase price of the dishwasher (on sale), and I do not have a working dishwasher. Stated another way, I have paid for nearly two new Maytag dishwashers since July 2019, yet as of October 2021, I am still washing all the dishes by hand, with no resolution in sight. I recommend to save up and buy a real dishwasher, or at least a brand that will continue to work after the 1-year warranty expires. The "10 YEAR Limited Parts Warranty" label that I see every time I look at the dishwasher mocks me, and I despise Maytag. This was my first and last Maytag appliance.

Update: On October 27, 2021, this is what Laura P. of the Maytag Consumer Care Team has to say about the parts for my two-year old dishwasher being on backorder with no estimated date of restocking:

"The unit is outside of the manufacturer's warranty and isn't under any recalls or known issues at this time."

In other words, if you buy a Maytag appliance, you are on your own. Too bad Virginia does not have a "right to repair" law for consumer products, which would compel the manufacturer to make the parts available for a reasonable number of years.

Since my recent contacts with Maytag, I have just begun receiving emails from Maytag's marketing department offering to sell me a Maytag Service Plan for my Maytag dishwasher through AIG WarrantyGuard, Inc. Maytag is "not affiliated" with AIG, but the email is from Maytag! I tried calling the phone number for "Questions" about the warranty service plan, but after a 10 minute hold, the call is terminated. This happened 3 times in a row. I was going to ask whether they are able to get repair parts that the Maytag factory authorized repair service cannot get! I doubt very much that the parts are available. Maytag is trying to squeeze more money out of me for a dishwasher that they know very well cannot be repaired unless and until the control panel becomes available, which may be never. The control panel is the most expensive part of the dishwasher, it is not covered by the 10 year parts warranty, and it was evidently not designed or built for long-term survivability. It can't be repaired because its design is proprietary. Since this two-year old dishwasher model is now obsolete (no doubt because it was poorly designed), so is the control panel!

For my washer, I had to cut the tube off in order for the wires to then fit between the back washer panel the the back top edge of the washer cabinet.  Leaving it on would have resulted in a bulge in the back panel.  The original inlet valve did NOT have the plastic tubing.  I installed the new valve in about 15 minutes.  Water filling temperatures are immediately back to normal.  We did two washer loads - working perfectly.  This was a great buy; saved a lot of $$$ vs a repair call.  And had faster service.

Reading all the other reviews of this product......you have to blame the error of the customers and not the product itself.

If you have ever owned a Wine Fridge.....you know it is NOT a refrigerator....that is not its purpose. If the other reviewers wanted a beverage holder that was able to keep food in it or keep beverages below 40degrees....then they should have gotten a REFRIGERATOR...not a wine fridge/chiller.

So knowing that....let us give an honest and realistic review of this item based on what it was actually designed for.

This unit while not the highest frills of wine chillers is attractive with a stainless steel trim on the door and a glass front and a black body. The door is reversible and it has an internal blue LED interior light you can turn on/off depending on your mood. It does not have a Temperature indicator with a simple dial for temperature with MIN to MAX indicators. It is simple and attractive.....and given its price....thats to be expected. I purchased a suction cup thermometer that faces out and mounts to the interior of the glass door for like 2$.

It comes with 4 adjustable racks and the nice bonus of a bottom storage area rack that has not been present in other wine chillers I have purchased. It allows you to stack cans on the bottom on their side so they don't roll out.

My unit is new and I purchased it as it is replacing an old Urbina thermoelectric wine chiller that finally crapped out after 2.5 years (It was dirt cheap so no big whoop). We will see if this unit is the exception.

Lets be honest......these units don't tend to last more than 3 years on average so if you are worried about that a higher end unit may be to your liking....but you will pay a pricey premium for actual fridge-like beverage centers like GE's.....or just invest in a long extended warranty so you can be re-imbursed should it fail within 3 years (this is what I did).

This unit unlike my old model has an actual compressor and sealed coolant system which is a luxury at this price range....usually you are getting a thermo-electric cooling system at prices below 200$.

I will update my review in the coming months but so far my unit on MAX is cooling better than expected with an average of 33F below room temp:
(Current Results = Room Temp - 75F / Cooler Temp - 42F )
* NOTE: Cooler is in a shaded corner away from direct sunlight...and this is also one of the 'newer' models in stores now.

Hopefully this informed and realistic review will help others. This is good unit for the price if you want a beverage chiller. It is similar to units they use at bars and convenience stores on or near the counter. Your beverages will be chilled but they will not be ice cold. Your white wine will be in the perfect temperature range (depending on the temp of your home or room)......which is exactly what this unit was designed for.

Many years ago, back in the 80’s, when I was finally out of school and living on my own, I bought and tried using a funnel gadget that was designed to make a single cup of coffee. It is now the current trend for generating pour-over drip coffee. It just never worked well. By the time all the water passed through the filter into my cup, it was barely warm, not to mention having to stir the grounds nearly constantly to keep it flowing. I eventually tossed it and have avoided similar products since.

Fast forward to today.. My husband and I try to travel as much as we can but in Europe, tea pots are the norm and hotel rooms simply don’t supply coffee makers. At restaurants, an order for coffee will give you one tiny cup of espresso with no refills. I’ve been looking for a solution that would allow me to use the hot water from the teapots to generate a cup of “Americano-style” coffee, and I’ve found it! This Vietnamese Coffee Maker from Ubenkaku works perfectly. And it is simple, no cords, no electricity required, and it’s small and lightweight, easy to pack or use at home.

I stumbled upon this little device that really works like a cross between the drip funnel style and french press. It has holes at the bottom of the “saucer”, and another panel that screws into the cup, and the coffee grounds are sandwiched between these two perforated panels. Once hot water is poured into the cup portion, a supplied lid can be placed on top to help retain the heat as the coffee drips through.

The holes are small but not small enough for an espresso grind, but will work well for the fineness used for regular drip coffee makers. I may occasionally be using espresso-ground coffee, so I cut paper coffee filters the size of the cup, placed it in first, then loaded the coffee. This works! It generates a cup of fairly strong coffee without a coffee mud in the bottom of the cup, which I can add more hot water to if I want my “Americano”. If k-cups are available, I can simply open the pod, dump the coffee in, then brew, no extra filter paper required.

This little maker has a taupe-colored powder-coated finish on the outside but has a brushed stainless finish on all parts that will be exposed to coffee or hot water. The outer finish is perfectly smooth and attractive. I had wondered if the thin handle or lid might get too hot to touch and they do not. The handle remains totally cool. The lid gets warm but not so warm that I can’t touch it.

I read a review that stated that this is difficult to clean due to the screw hole (that holds the filter in place), but I don’t find it difficult at all. My preference is to make a fairly strong mini-cup of coffee, then add more water to my desired strength, which changes based on time of day. This wonderful little gadget will be used at home and packed in luggage for all future travel!

I hope you found this review to be helpful. Thanks for reading!!

I'm not sure if the existing start relay and capacitor failed due to age (13+ yrs) or due to lightning from storms the previous night, all I know is that when I got up Monday morning my Frigidaire refrigerator (model # FRS6LR5EM6) didn't sound normal.  I could hear the compressor try to engage, run for a few seconds and then make a distinct "click" and then the compressor would stop.  I feared having to spend $1000+ on a new fridge so I did a web search and found that the most common cause for the clicking noise was a bad starter/capacitor.  I searched the model and found the part number and then went straight to Amazon.  Around 36 hours later I had a new Start Relay and Capacitor and then installed them with no issues.  Luckily we had a 2nd fridge in our garage to hold our food in the meantime.  I took the opportunity to clean 13 years work of dust from the coils and fan.  After I installed the part I plugged in the fridge, flipped the breaker and crossed my fingers.  Success!  The compressor roared to life and the fridge immediately started cooling down.  As of this morning it's back to operating temps and the compressor is cycling normally with no "clicking" noises.  If your fridge is having similar issues do yourself a favor and look up the correct Starter/Capacitor, replace it yourself and save lots of money! There are lots of videos online to show you exactly how to do it. Remember to unplug your appliance before doing any service!

September 3, 2013 edit:

After fairly heavy use over the past two weeks, I've found exactly one weak point. The thin plastic piece supporting the steel mesh basket can and will warp, causing the mesh itself to get "crushed" if less-than-gentle hands try emptying the Ekobrew while it's still hot. This wasn't a problem for me, since I usually wait for the grounds to cool off, but after letting some coworkers use it I noticed it was misshapen. Keep in mind, however, that mine was being used at least ten times a day, and often back-to-back by two or three different people.

While this affects the clean look of the Ekobrew, it does nothing to detract from its functionality, and even if the "beatings" continued I have few doubts this would last for the duration of my deployment. If you want to avoid getting the slightly crushed look mine now sports, simply tap lightly on the reinforced sides after it's cooled off. I wouldn't consider this a design flaw so much as a lack of user training, so the Ekobrew maintains its five-star rating in my book!

I purchased this because my washing machine is broken and the needed repair or replacement was not feasible at the moment and the laundromat in my area is a little scary. I feel it cleans the clothes as well as the regular washer does. I filled an empty hand soap bottle with my laundry detergent and just use one pump to wash the clothes which works perfectly. My regular washer is an XL capacity and it usually takes me 3-4 loads in this washer to equal 1 usual load in my regular washer.

In this washer I usually use the normal setting and wash for 9 minutes, then transfer and spin for 1 minute. After that I do a rinse for 3 minutes and then a final spin, just for 1 minute again as that removes the water to a comparable dryness as the spin cycle on my regular washer.

Now that I'm used to using it it's much easier to tell how much you can put in it, but every once in a while I get one article of clothing too many and it has a hard time agitating so I have to remove something. But it really fits more than I expected which I am happy about.

The cons:
The spinner side much smaller than the washer side. For each one load you wash, you have to divide it in half and do two spin cycles which is a real pain. That's the biggest issue I have with the washer.

It's very easy to make the load not quite balanced, especially in the spin cycle which causes the machine to rock back and forth so you have to watch it closely while spinning. That might not be as big of an issue if you are using it in the tub or shower, but when it's on the counter it's a problem.

There's no fill line for the water in the washer even though the instruction manual says to fill to the fill line. I've seen several comments mentioning filling the water to the little cut out hole at the top back of the washer, but if you fill it that high it spills into the other side, Also, The manual refers to a lint trap, but there isn't one.

The last thing is that every time when done using there's a very small amount of black rubbery stuff on the counter underneath. I can only presume it comes from the belts on the washer or spinner which makes me worried they will break and I don't know if they can be replaced or if that will be the end of the washer. It has happened since the very first load I washed which only had two shirts to test it, so I know it's not from overloading it.

Overall, I really love the washer and would definitely recommend it. I'm happy I bought it and would buy it again.

After 7 seasons of removing water from my dehumidifiers by hand I was ready to try a product like this.

The idea behind this product is simple.It works on the same principle as a sump pump.When the water reaches a certain point in the pumps well area,a quick burst of pumping action causes the water to flow up a hose and out to wherever you route the end of the hose-in my case through a drilled hole outside my basement area to the outside of my house.

Installation was easy enough.I simply cut the hose to my needed length,attached it to the unit,attached the other hose connection to my dehumidifiers hose connector (for condensation that comes out of the actual dehumidifier) and plugged the unit in.Let me mention(no laughing please)that I broke my nose during this simple installation by having too tight of a hole drilled to the outside for the outtake hose.I was pulling the hose with a needle nose plier to pull through the hole and ended up smashing my nose when the plier slipped and my knuckle came smashing on to my nose.I needed a nose job anyway...

Anyway,the unit works really well and now I can leave home for days at a time and know that my basement is at a safe 45% humidity level.Without the unit turned on it would be twice that amount at least.

Just be aware that the dehumidifier pump needs to be physically lower than the dehumidifier.The gravity will force the condensation down the hose in to the dehumidifier pump.I made the mistake of leaving both level with each other and found the the water was just building up and began running out on the the floor.

Besides the pliers hitting my face (I`ll remember it every time that pump turns itself on) and having to figure out that gravity needs to be used to make things work correctly, I am so happy with the results. If it lasts a few years it will be worth the 96 $ (shipping included) I paid for the pump.

Editors note- It is now Oct of 09` and the pump continues to work perfectly. It has been on for the last two seasons (Apr-Oct of 08 and 09) and still no problems.

2nd editors note-It`s now May 2011 and unit still working perfectly

My old brackets are plastic (these are spring metal with a hole in the center!) so I carefully bent and broke off the remaining bracket and a half. This part has a nearly identical twin, and the key difference is in the size and shape of the terminals on the solenoids. If your current part has four bare electrical lugs (of which two connect to white pieces, and two to black) and a gray piece for the hose connection, then this is NOT the one you want. If your current part has two electrical connections (one white, one yellow, each with two wires) and a yellow-ish piece for the hose connection, then you're all set.

The plastic bits all appear to come from the same mold, and the solenoids are stamped with identical specs by the same manufacturer, but the difference in the electrical connections can trip you up. You can guess how I came upon this knowledge.

I made a simple modifications to seal off that gap by putting a small rubber band (like the produce bands from the grocery store) around the top. I have ordered some paper filter inserts and will see if that works even better, but even without them this was more than acceptable. I have used some other reusable cups that use a mesh screen, and those let a lot of sediment through. This was much better.

Bottom line is, if you are planning on using this with a B or K series machine with the cup holder that has the indentations, then you are going to want to modify it a bit to keep it from leaking. When it does work though, it works pretty well.

I used an air hose with a nozzle on the second attempt to blow all the frozen ice out of the drain line.  I think I was just a little too quick turning the fridge back on; should have let it thaw out longer.  Sure beats buying a new fridge or paying a repairman hundreds to fix. Recommend buying if you are somewhat handy and watch the YouTube how-to videos.

First off:

- I am NOT an electrician
- I am NOT an HVAC guy
- I am a troubleshooter and a DIY'er

Here's the story. 10-year old Whirlpool freezer wasn't keeping up, moisture was showing on items, and the ice wasn't fully frozen when it tumbled out of the icemaker. Initial basic troubleshooting included vacuuming up all the dust from the grill, the back, and the condenser coils (which were loaded down w/ dust). At first, the compressor would fire up, but then gradually - the freezing problems continued and all I heard from the unit was clicking after clicking.

My thoughts were: 1.) The door seals are leaking 2.) There is a signal problem 3.) The compressor is gone.

I didn't think the seals were a problem and the compressor WOULD fire up periodically, so my hunch was that wasn't it. After stopping to YouTube a few times, I took the plate off the back, located the relay that was clicking, detached it, shook it gently, and heard rattling (which based on the YouTubes I saw indicated it was bad). So I googled for replacement parts and actually found the original pieces (for ~$100) or the 3-in-1 relay (for $10). My idea was - let's try this and see if it works, if it doesn't - well, I'll just have to accept having to buy a new unit.

So it arrived in the mail, I detached the wires that were connected to the relay and hooked up the parts based on the instructions (which are super duper easy). The longest part was stripping and connecting the wires since, well....I'm not an electrician and don't do it very often. Finally after assembly (~15 minutes or so), I plugged the fridge back in and waited for the moment of truth....and BOOM.....Soft metal humming of the compressor !!! I actually waited for the unit to run several cycles before I wrote this column.

A little troubleshooting, some scientific method, and finger-crossing and she's up and running again. Saved me at least $500 in a repair (and probably the "offer" of a new compressor). And of course......didn't have to buy a fridge !!

We had issues with the washer leaking soapy water. Doing some research on the internet showed this happens the dispenser cup is no longer siphoning all of the water and soap as part of the wash cycle. Then when the rinse cycle starts, the dispenser cup fills with water again and soapy water is added to the rinse water. This makes the rinse water soapy. And when this soapy rinse water is combined with the already soapy clothes it creates excess soap foam. This excess foam goes out the overflow vent in the back middle of the washer, and out onto the floor.

The dispenser cup losses the ability to siphon when the seal between the white fill indicator and the shaft fails as pieces start deforming.

To test if have this issue, fill your current dispenser TO THE TOP with water. It should start draining water out of the drain hole on the bottom, and drain almost all of the water from the dispenser If not, get this item and your problems will be solved!

These wheels are an excellent replacement for the OEM wheels that come off the lower dish rack.  Mine lasted almost 3 years, which is longer than most judging from review comments.  (It appears the OEM glue cannot withstand the heat from the dishwasher, and the axles holding the wheels come off.)  These replacement parts have a stainless steel axle and screw, which will hopefully be much longer lasting than the plastic ones that are glued on.  I have a Kenmore Elite dishwasher Model No. 665.1482 or 665.1483.  The wheels assembly is OEM part no. WPW10195417 or W10195417.  This replacement part is the tall version (about 3-1/2 inches from the bottom of the wheel to the top of the housing).  This extra height (many of the replacement wheel assemblies are only about 2-3/4 inches from the bottom of the wheel to the top of the housing) is needed to allow the dishwasher spray arm to operate and not hit the bottom rack on my Kenmore Elite dishwasher.  This is very reasonably priced too, about 1/8 the cost of the ridiculously overpriced OEM replacement parts (which are still the ones with plastic axles that are glued on and likely won't last very long)!  I gave it 4 stars because it doesn't roll smoothly when the lower rack is empty (some of the wheels don't turn), but it rolls much better when the lower rack is loaded.  Overall, this replacement wheel assembly is an upgrade to the OEM version (stainless steel axle screwed on vs. plastic axle glued on) at about 1/8 the price.

I am writing this as someone who finds themselves in a place for the first time without a washer and dryer, someone who is short and doesn't have a lot of strength, and...as someone who was very nervous to make this purchase, but glad she did!

I've had this for about 2 weeks now. I was very worried to purchase this, because I thought it wouldn't work. After reading reviews on here and watching a ton of youtube videos (while at the laundromat!), I decided to buy it and I was NOT disappointed! I have ran this maybe about 8 times already.

I have a few comments that were not covered in review videos:

-If you are a single person, such as myself, do your laundry once a week. Do NOT let your laundry pile up, or you could very well be doing laundry for HOURS.

-The above may seem like a no-brainer, but what they don't tell you is that because the wash time and spin time are so short, be prepared to basically babysit this thing. 15 minutes can go by very quickly, then you're off to start loading the spin cycle..

-Which brings me to my next comment, and why this did not get a full 5 stars from me - the spin cycle capacity drum is very tiny! Why they didn't make it the same size is beyond me! This has been the most annoying/frustrating part, and why I say you have to babysit your machine.
Normally 1 washing load takes me 3 loads to put in the spin cycle, and the spin cycle only lasts 5 minutes. And maybe 5 minutes isn't enough sometimes (although that 5 minutes is as powerful as most people say, and I'm amazed every time how mostly dry they are). It is NOT that I am overloading - but for example, you're not going to want to put a towel and 2 pairs of pants in the spin cycle - the towel will probably be enough to go in on its own.

-Prepared to get wet.
As you see, most people fill it up first before putting clothes in, which means you have to plunge your laundry down. Before they go into the spin cycle, obviously they are sopping wet, which you're not used to with a normal washer.

Tips
-If you are not going to put this in your bathtub or shower, make sure it is elevated for draining. I've seen people use a small table or crates. Unless you are using this outside, you cannot just have it flat on the floor and try to drain it in a bucket without it being elevated - it will not drain, it uses gravity.

-I found a brilliant hack for using the water tube from a video on youtube - get a rubber glove, snip off the tip of a finger, and put the hose through it. Secure with rubber band. Put glove over the shower head and secure with another rubber band. Easy peasy!

-I have not done this yet, but it was suggested to get a lint catcher ball, and I've seen people use those spiky dryer balls in there for more agitation.

-If your clothes are very soiled, it's best to pre-wash them by hand to work on any stains.

-Detergent pods DO work and disintegrate in this!

-Even if you normally don't, use fabric softener. It helps.

Final thoughts:
This washer has already paid for itself for the hassle it saves me from loading up my laundry and going to the laundromat (which is worse when you have stairs!) I wouldn't say it saves me time, but it gives me the freedom of being comfortable in my home instead of a laundromat. But realistically, this is not the end-all be-all. As long as you don't expect that, you are going to be very happy. I knew buying this that I'm still going to have to go to the laundromat for my comforter and big items, and I'm fine with that.

The spin cycle truly is amazing and wrings out your clothes 90%. But this is not a heated dryer. For some reason, portable dryers are twice this cost, but they do exist!

For myself being short and not having much strength, I am able to lift this into the bathtub. I suggest surveying your apartment for where you are going to store this first before buying - luckily my small dining room has enough space to store this while not in use.

I am lucky that I don't pay water at my complex, which is why I felt I definitely needed to try this, but I have read in reviews that people's water bills do go up with this, so be forewarned.

Hope this helps!

This device is a very simple one and I like it. You connect the included wall plate and plastic 'el' to the outside of the house and place the canister included on top. There is a cap inside of the canister which lifts when the air is flowing and vents the air downward. The photo in the seller's listing is a bit misleading as you might think that the top of the canister would be the thing that opens allowing hot air to exit from the top. The lid at the top is for cleaning and normally will remain closed.

The flange unit which attaches to the wall (upon which the working canister is placed) is minimally wider than the typical hooded vent so make sure you have a bit of extra space to accomodate it . You could probably take a 1/2" off each side of it with a band saw and simply caulk it to the wall if the fit was close enough.

--

Things to consider-

-The dryer needs to hang to use the bag feature. Depending on where the outlet is the cord length may be an issue. It would be best to travel with a small extension cord just in case.

Noticed 2011 Maytag top freezer refrigerator suddenly wasn't as cold as usual, but freezer was cold as ever. Area around base of duct rear center of freezer compartment was iced up, fan inside duct not running. Quick google and youtube confirmed dead evaporator fan would cause the exact scenario. No instructions included, but none really needed. Only tool necessary a 1/4" hex nut driver. Unplugged unit, removed shelf rack, ice maker and rear panel inside freezer compartment. Removed fan bracket assembly and separated back from front by squeezing clips. Removed fan from old motor. Pulls straight off, but requires a little force; fan is flexible plastic so minimal chance of breakage, just grasp center hub only. Transferred silicone rubber grommet from old to new motor shaft, then mounted in and reassembled bracket and reinstalled on back wall of freezer compartment. Pressed fan fully onto shaft and reinstalled rear interior panel and ice maker. Plugged unit back in and voila! 10 minute job. Next morning, refrigerator compartment a chilly 38 degrees again.

I have an older Whirlpool ED25TEXHW02 Side by Side Refrigerator with ice maker and separate in door ice / water dispensers. At first I noticed water freezing in the ice maker water supply tupe, then "hollow ice cubes". Researched how it all works online and came to the right conclusion is was the valve / solenoid assembly (after first coming the wrong conclusion is was the ice maker and replacing it) and found an excellent price plus FREE SHIPPING here. Whoppee ! It works. Took about 30 minutes to replace old assembly - and about 20 minutes to run 3 gallons of water through after the work (to get the air out of the lines).

My original assembly used all compression fittings. This unit use all but 2 "push a plug" connectors for the water lines. I was worried if I had to cut the compression fitting off the line would be too short - so the ones that slid right off I took off and left the other compression fittings on the line (it's better than cutting the line too short). Piece of cake - no cutting any plastic lines, they all fit fine. I was worried about the main water inlet - my supply line is copper with a brass compression washer and nut. Not a problem - the main water inlet on the new assembly is metal.

NOTE: BEFORE disconnecting the wire connectors on the original assembly - note which terminal on the solenoids the colored wire goes to. Each solenoid has a tab marked with an alpha / numeric indicator (A1 or B4) and an alpha indicator (L or M). All the white wires should go to the same label indicator on all the solenoids. So it's simple - for example only: Just remember - "white to A1 (or B4)" and your have it licked. You shouldn't have a problem reassembling and putting the wrong connector the the wrong solenoid - the tabs on the two solenoids are different sizes. The main water inlet solenoid connector is almost always colored Red.

Have fun, and best of luck to all!

Signal strength is above 90% according to the app but sensors will not report for hours. Sensors are between 15 to 30ft away and on different floors, but no correlation to the failures.

The alerts are slow, I'll get a text alert at 8:30am for an event that happened at 6:30am according to the text. Charts in the app and online work but the x-axis is a pretty useless serious of random timestamps for a chart that spans 4-5 days. Touching the charts will highlight datapoints with temp and time, but no date. No ability to zoom or scroll through time. You can download a CSV file of the data via the website, but when I tried to download the file it occasionally gave me an empty CSV file with just a single row of headers. When it works it appears to have all the data going back months.

All in all useful product, but if you need something guaranteed reliable you might want to look elsewhere.
